title: Bad Beat of the Week: an Under undone in overtime
summary: Tied 6–6 after three quarters, Cleveland and New Orleans finished 23–22 in overtime. The 45 combined points beat a documented pregame Under 42.5 ticket by 2.5 points.
preview: A November 6 snapshot showed just 22% of tickets but 92% of money on Under 42.5; those percentages were not closing splits.

title: A trophy night, then a drone
summary: A drone interruption paused Thursday night football at Lambeau Field. The Brewers also brought their World Series trophy to the game; the shared evening is documented, not a demonstrated connection.
preview: Yahoo’s broadcast account reports a Josh Jacobs touchdown reception on the next play.

title: When exactly was the play over?
summary: Devonte Wyatt’s personal foul extended a Detroit possession during a 20–17 Green Bay loss. Players disputed whether the play had ended; the referee said it had.
preview: Detroit scored a touchdown to lead 17–14.

title: Five wins. Five late escapes.
summary: Cleveland’s 27–24 win over Tennessee extended an unusual start: each of its first five wins featured the winning score in the final four minutes of regulation or overtime.
preview: The published comparison identifies the 2016 Lions as the other team to do this since 1970.

title: The Coach’s night. A familiar opponent.
summary: Chicago’s first home game after Mike Ditka’s death brought New England to Soldier Field—the same opponent his Bears beat in Super Bowl XX. The Bears honored him before a 30–24 win.
preview: A moment of silence, No. 89 tributes, and a 30–24 Chicago win against Ditka’s Super Bowl opponent.

title: A touchdown and a takeaway
summary: Travis Hunter caught a touchdown and intercepted a pass in the same game. Jacksonville’s team report identifies it as the first such NFL performance since 2002.
preview: Jacksonville tied it at 31 before Houston won 34–31.

title: A field goal that never happened
summary: Washington reached field-goal territory in overtime, then ran out of time without attempting a kick. The Giants escaped with a 27–27 tie.
preview: Washington could not organize another snap. No winning field goal was attempted.

title: Eight seconds were enough
summary: Philadelphia took a late lead in London, but a returnable kickoff gave Jacksonville the field position for Cam Little’s winning 57-yard field goal. The Jaguars won 19–17.
preview: Little converted from 57 yards to win.

title: One yard. A very short field.
summary: Leading 17–10, the Chargers failed on fourth-and-1 at their own 41. Denver tied the game on the ensuing short field and eventually won 23–17.
preview: Denver scored a tying touchdown; later Herbert turnovers preceded two field goals.

title: Just get to halftime
summary: A Seattle rushing play near its own goal line became a San Francisco fumble-recovery touchdown just before halftime. The Seahawks lost 32–29.
preview: San Francisco led 21–13. Seattle had given up three first-half touchdowns after turnovers.

title: An upright changes the ticket
summary: Miami’s late touchdown made it a seven-point game, but Riley Patterson missed the extra point. Cincinnati’s 31–24 win covered a documented -6.5 line by half a point.

title: The no-call, then the suspension
summary: A disputed third-down non-call was followed by an official’s confrontation with Trey McBride. The NFL subsequently suspended line judge Jeff Seeman for two games.
preview: The league announced a two-game suspension for unprofessional conduct.

title: The winning play that lost the spread
summary: T.J. Hockenson stopped short of the end zone so Minnesota could finish in victory formation. The Vikings won 15–10, leaving a documented -10.5 spread uncovered.
preview: Minnesota used kneel-downs to end the game.

title: Too early for victory formation?
summary: Trevor Lawrence stopped near the goal line with more than eight minutes left. New England used a timeout, and Bhayshul Tuten scored on the next play in Jacksonville’s 35–6 win.
preview: After a Patriots timeout, Tuten ran for the touchdown.

title: The rule hiding in plain sight
summary: Cameron Dicker made a 57-yard fair-catch kick with no time left in the first half. The rare option helped Los Angeles on the way to a 34–27 win.
preview: Dicker made the 57-yard attempt with no defensive rush.
